name: Private relay
blurb: A rack in a harbour data hall, leased under a name that is not yours. It goes into your address book as a relay that slows a trace more than any open one, and it never warms up however often you use it.

name: Safe house
blurb: A second address with a line of its own. A trace that gets home finds this one: you lie low half as long, the heat on you fades twice as fast, and no trace burns a part out of your gateway again.

name: Second gateway
blurb: A second rig racked beside the first and wired to share the load: one more connection at a time, two more programs running at once, and 16 GB more memory to load.

name: Core loft
blurb: A loft of second-hand cores wired to watch your programs work. The shortcuts you do by hand play themselves: lit letters are caught, the proxy's real address is named and the decrypter's key is turned. A quick hand is still a little quicker.

name: Night desk
blurb: Three people on a night shift who tidy up after you. When you walk out of a server, the lines that would give you away are scrubbed for you, and no log review finds anything.

name: Cut-out
blurb: A paid name that stands between you and the world. Once a day, a trace that gets home finds the cut-out and not you: no fine, no heat, no lying low, no lost rating. The connection still drops, and that server changes its locks.
